Leading zeros on a bare feed entry read as decimal (not octal) and are stripped; 0 and 00 are the same octet.
Trailing text after the address is cut at the first space or #; whole-line comment markers (#, !, //) and blank lines yield nothing.
Whitespace shapes around an address: CRLF, tabs, runs of spaces, NBSP and BOM at the edge, a lone \r.
a-b ranges expand to the minimal CIDR cover; malformed and reversed ranges.

cases.description: A range on a feed with suppression: each expanded CIDR is sanitized on its own, with the floor message.
iBlocklist/PeerGuardian p2p lines: "<Org>:<start>-<end>" split at the last colon (issue #1923); lines that merely contain - and : are left alone.
An auto-typed "IP/path" line: the bare host is recovered, the first path segment is never a mask (issue #1933).
Opposite-family and non-address lines on a v4 list: silent unless the line looks numeric.
DShield start<TAB>end<TAB>prefix rows: one exact CIDR is taken, anything inconsistent falls through to the two-host extract (issue #2604).

A URL host or bare token longer than 253 characters is never split into labels.
Whole-line IPv4-mapped IPv6 on a v4 list: decoded once, with and without a mask, case and spacing.
Regex parser: addresses are pulled out of hosts-style, CSV, HTML and prose lines; duplicates on a line collapse (array_unique), order kept.
Regex parser ranges: the first a-b pair is expanded and the rest of the line ignored; failed expansions are counted.
A regex range on a feed with suppression on: suppressed expansions are counted failures.
Regex parser, hostile shapes: edge whitespace, quotes, a stray 0xFF byte, shell and regex metacharacters, NUL, BOM, a 300-character host.
The regex parser on plain address lines: CIDR masks kept, /0 clamped, loopback kept when suppression is off.

cases.description: IPv6 masks on a custom list: /0 kept as written, :: still rejected (issue #1922).
IPv6 lines with comments and edge whitespace on the auto parser: the cut keeps its trailing space in the logged line.
A v4 line on a v6 list is silent; a bare numeric one counts.
IPv6 a-b ranges: the minimal CIDR cover, canonical output; reversed, equal and malformed pairs.
IPv6 ranges on a feed with suppression: expanded CIDRs that sanitize away set the suppressed flag.
IPv6 DShield-style tab rows: one exact CIDR is taken, inconsistent rows fall through to the two-host extract; the opposite family is left alone.
IPv6 tab rows on a feed with suppression: the declared CIDR is sanitized (suppressed flag, floor message).
IPv6 regex parser: addresses pulled out of prose and markup; duplicates collapse; a %zone swallows the rest of its line; # cuts a match.
IPv6 regex parser, hostile shapes: invalid UTF-8, BOM, quotes, metacharacters, oversized lines.
IPv6 regex parser on a feed with suppression and a floor: dropped matches set the suppressed flag.
IPv4-mapped entries on a v6 list never match a packet: dropped and counted (auto parser).
IPv4-mapped entries on a v6 list never match a packet: dropped and counted (regex parser).
NUL bytes in v6 lines: a token cut by a NUL is dropped, NUL at a token edge stays a boundary, NUL alone is not a counted failure (auto parser).
NUL bytes in v6 lines: a token cut by a NUL is dropped, NUL at a token edge stays a boundary, NUL alone is not a counted failure (regex parser).
The same NUL lines with suppression on.
NUL at a range endpoint of a v4 line falls through to the regex extract; NUL inside a tab row falls through to the two-host extract.

types.description: A regex-format list is always parsed with the regex parser, whatever its URL.
A .txt feed is auto.
A URL without a dot in its last path segment has no extension, which reads as empty: regex.
A bare host URL: the last segment is the host, whose extension is the TLD.
.html is regex.
.htm is regex.
.php is regex.
.aspx is regex.
.cgi is regex.
.csv is regex.
.rules is regex.
A trailing dot is an empty extension: regex.
The extension compare is case-sensitive: .HTML is auto.
.json is auto.
.gz is auto.
.zip is auto.
A query after the extension is cut: .php?x=1 is php, regex.
A query after .txt is cut: auto.
The extension is read after the last dot of the whole last segment, query included: ?v=1.html is html.
A query without a dot leaves no extension: regex.
A trailing slash is ignored by basename: list.php/ is php.
An iblocklist URL is auto even when its path ends in .php.
An iblocklist host forces auto over a .csv extension.
iblocklist in the directory part only (not in the file name) counts.
iblocklist in the file name only does not.
A dot in the directory part is not the extension.
A dot in the directory part with a .txt file: auto.
userinfo and port do not matter: .txt is auto.
A fragment is part of the last segment: list.txt#a.csv reads csv, regex.
A dot-file name reads its text as the extension: .txt is auto.
A local path: dirname "." and no extension: regex.
A local file name: auto.
An empty URL has neither directory nor extension: regex.
regex format beats the iblocklist rule.
Any format other than regex is treated as auto-capable: .txt is auto.
Repeated slashes: the segment after the last slash.
A URL of slashes only: no segment, regex.
